title: Valuation Basis for Losses under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan
content:
The loss is valued before anything is owed under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan, and what the plan accepts is the appraised cost of repair or replacement, never the amount the host asked for.

### How the loss may be valued

A claim worth more than the plan's photo estimate threshold cannot be settled on photographs and goes to an in-person adjuster or a repair shop invoice; a claim at or below the threshold may be settled on photographs alone.

### Ceilings

> Retired clause: "The accepted amount is capped twice over, first by the sublimit for the kind of loss and then by the plan's overall physical damage limit, and the lower of the two governs." This clause is no longer in force and no accepted amount is settled on it.

The remainder of that provision stands unchanged: sublimits are not added together where one loss spans several kinds of damage, each kind being capped on its own.

### Total loss

Where the appraised cost reaches the plan's total loss threshold as a percentage of the marketplace valuation of the vehicle, the claim is settled as a total loss at that valuation less the deductible rather than as a repair.

### Loss of use

> Retired clause: "Loss of use is paid at the plan's daily rate for the days the vehicle is genuinely off the road, up to the plan's maximum." This clause is no longer in force.

What remains of that provision is in force and governs the plans that carry no such benefit: loss of use is not paid at all on plans that carry no loss of use benefit, and a benefit the plan does not carry is not paid at a reduced rate. Where a plan publishes no daily sum for loss of use, nothing at all is payable under that head on that plan.

### Further cost after the appraisal

Further cost found after the appraisal is added as a supplement only inside the plan's supplement window and only up to the plan's supplement ceiling as a percentage of the original appraisal; cost found later, or beyond the ceiling, is refused rather than opened as a fresh claim. The supplement window is counted from the day of the appraisal standing on the claim, read from that claim's own appraisal record, and a supplement brought on the last day of the window is still inside it.

### Exclusions that stand on every plan

Wear, ordinary cleaning and mechanical failure with no trip event behind it are excluded on every plan, and a plan that includes mechanical cover still excludes failure that would have happened whoever was driving.

### The marketplace's open exposure

The open exposure carried on a host is the total the appraisals have accepted on that host's claims that have been appraised and not yet paid, read as the portfolio stands on the day it is looked at.
